meaning: Make the most of the present time and give little thought to the future.
anecdote: This phrase originates from the first book of the Odes by the Roman poet Horace, published in 23 BC. The complete line is 'carpe diem, quam minimum credula postero,' which translates to 'Seize the day, put very little trust in tomorrow.' The historical context reflects the Epicurean philosophy popular in ancient Rome, which emphasized enjoying life's fleeting pleasures in the face of inevitable mortality.
prompt: How can you fully embrace the present moment without sacrificing your responsibilities to the future?
